title: StratSim: Theoretical Frameworks, Mathematical Formulations & Assumptions
courseContext: Principles of Management & Economics (POME) - Undergraduate / MBA Core

theories.name: BCG Growth-Share Matrix
theories.formula: Relative Market Share (RMS) = Firm Revenue / Leading Competitor Revenue. (Logarithmic scale). Market Growth Rate = YoY GMV/Revenue Expansion (%).

quadrants.Stars: High Growth (>20%), High Relative Share (>1.0). Requires heavy capex to defend lead; self-sustaining or near break-even.
quadrants.Cash Cows: Low Growth (<20%), High Relative Share (>1.0). Generates surplus cash to fund other ventures; harvest margins.
quadrants.Question Marks: High Growth (>20%), Low Relative Share (<1.0). High cash drain; dilemma between heavy investment to build or divesting.
quadrants.Dogs: Low Growth (<20%), Low Relative Share (<1.0). Weak competitive positioning; prime candidate for restructuring or harvest/exit.

theories.assumptions: Market share correlates with cumulative operational experience (Experience Curve) and purchasing scale discounts.

theories.name: Porter's Five Forces & Industry Attractiveness Index
theories.pioneer: Michael E. Porter, Harvard Business School (1979, 2008)
theories.formula: Attractiveness Index = 10 - \sum_{i=1}^{5} (w_i \cdot S_i) / \sum_{i=1}^{5} w_i, where S_i \in [1, 10] represents force hostility and w_i is force weight.
theories.interpretation: Scores range from 0 (hyper-competitive, zero economic profit) to 10 (benign monopoly/monopolistic profit haven). An index between 2.0 and 4.0 indicates an industry with intense rivalry and value capture compressed by buyers and suppliers.
theories.assumptions: Industry structure drives long-run average profitability across firms irrespective of individual operational effectiveness.

theories.name: Oligopolistic Pricing & Constant-Elasticity Demand System
theories.formula: Q_i(P_i, \mathbf{P}_{-i}) = A_i \cdot P_i^{-\epsilon_{ii}} \cdot \prod_{j \neq i} P_j^{\epsilon_{ij}}. Total Profit \Pi_i = Q_i \cdot (P_i - c_i) - F_i.
theories.nashEquilibrium: A price vector \mathbf{P}^* where no individual firm can increase \Pi_i by unilaterally altering P_i given competitors' prices.
theories.assumptions: Consumers make rational trade-offs between delivery price and speed. Cross-price elasticity \epsilon_{ij} capture consumer multi-homing degree.

theories.name: Organizational Architecture & POSDCORB
theories.pioneer: Luther Gulick & Lyndall Urwick (1937), Max Weber (1922), Tom Burns & G.M. Stalker (1961)
theories.formula: Hierarchical Layers L = \lceil \frac{\ln(\text{Headcount})}{\ln(\text{Span of Control})} \rceil. Coordination Cost Index = \text{Headcount} \cdot L \cdot \left(\frac{\text{Centralization \%}}{100}\right) \cdot \left(1 + \frac{\text{Formalization}}{10}\right) \cdot 10^{-3}.
theories.contingencySpectrum: Mechanistic Score = 0.5 \cdot \text{Centralization \%} + 5.0 \cdot \text{Formalization}. Scores > 65 classify as Mechanistic Bureaucracy; < 45 classify as Organic Agile Network.
theories.assumptions: Information distortion increases exponentially with each management layer (Fayol's Scalar Chain principle).

theories.name: Monte Carlo Uncertainty Propagation
theories.formula: 1,000 randomized draws: \tilde{S}_i = \text{clamp}(S_i + \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_S^2), 1, 10), \tilde{\epsilon} = \epsilon + \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\epsilon^2). Empirical 5th and 95th percentiles computed from sorted simulation distributions.
theories.assumptions: Uncertainty parameters follow bounded Gaussian distributions reflecting macro volatility and survey estimation variance.

limitations: Quick commerce is undergoing rapid daily price experimentation; baseline figures represent FY24 estimates.
Dark store geographic distribution has local sub-monopolies not fully captured by city-wide aggregation.
Rider labor supply elasticity is subject to localized seasonal and weather shocks.
